_comment: Not 100bb minus a bit. What changes at this depth:
- The 5-bet node disappears. A 4-bet is committing or all-in, so there is
no decision after it and vs_5Bet is not modelled here.
- 4-betting is jam-or-fold. After open 2.5 and a 3-bet to 9, hero has 31
behind into a 12.5 pot - under 1.5 SPR. There is no 4-bet-and-fold.
- Implied-odds hands lose most. Small pairs and weak suited connectors
need depth to pay off; high-card strength holds its value. Ranges
tighten at the bottom rather than uniformly.
- 3-bets get more linear, because bluffing needs fold equity you keep
past the flop and at 40bb you are usually already committed.

source.detail: Hand-authored from standard 40bb 6-max principles. NOT solver output - reasonable reference ranges, not an equilibrium. Replace with solver exports when available.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Folded to Hero in UTG. Open to 2.5bb or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 22+, ATs+, A5s-A4s, KTs+, QTs+, JTs, T9s, 98s, ATo+, KQo

explanations.RAISE: Shallower stacks mean less to win when a speculative hand connects, so the weakest suited connectors come out relative to 100bb while the broadways and pairs stay. UTG still opens into five players.
explanations.FOLD: Five players to act and only 40bb behind. Hands that needed implied odds to justify an UTG open no longer get paid enough when they hit.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Folded to Hero in MP. Open to 2.5bb or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 22+, A9s+, A5s-A3s, K9s+, Q9s+, J9s+, T8s+, 98s, 87s, ATo+, KJo+, QJo

explanations.RAISE: One fewer player than UTG, so the suited aces and suited gappers come in. The small suited connectors below 87s stay out at this depth - they are implied-odds hands and the implied odds are not there.
explanations.FOLD: Four players left to act. Without depth to pay off a well-disguised hand, marginal holdings have to fold.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Folded to Hero in CO. Open to 2.5bb or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 22+, A2s+, K8s+, Q9s+, J9s+, T8s+, 97s+, 87s, 76s, A9o+, KTo+, QTo+, JTo

explanations.RAISE: Three players left, two of them blinds, so stealing starts to pay. Every suited ace opens for the blocker and nut-flush value, which matter just as much short as deep.
explanations.FOLD: Two players still have position. Weak offsuit hands play badly heads-up out of position and cannot make up for it with postflop maneuvering at this depth.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Folded to Hero on the Button. Open to 2.5bb or fold.

explanations.RAISE: Still the widest range at the table. Only the blinds remain and we have position for the rest of the hand - that edge does not shrink with stack depth, so the Button stays aggressive.
explanations.FOLD: Even here, offsuit hands with a low card and no straight potential make no pair, no draw and no fold equity.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Folded to Hero in the SB. Open to 3bb or fold.

explanations.RAISE: Heads-up against one player who must fold often, but out of position for the whole hand. A raise-or-fold strategy at 3bb; limping is a separate approach not modelled here.
explanations.FOLD: Out of position against a Big Blind who defends wide. Without depth to outplay them later, a hand needs to make something by itself.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. UTG opens to 2.5bb, folded to Hero in the BB. 3-bet to 9bb, call 1.5bb more, or fold.

explanations.RAISE: A 3-bet at this depth commits a quarter of the stack, so it is for value against a tight range rather than a bluff. The hands that want all the money in.
explanations.CALL: We close the action at better than 3-to-1, which is as good short as it is deep. But a hand must make something on its own - the implied odds that justified calling with weak suited hands at 100bb are gone.
explanations.FOLD: Against the tightest opening range at the table, with 40bb and no implied odds, most hands cannot show a profit even at this price.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. MP opens to 2.5bb, folded to Hero in the BB. 3-bet to 9bb, call 1.5bb more, or fold.

explanations.RAISE: MP opens wider than UTG, so value widens with it. The suited wheel aces are the one bluff that still works short - they block the hands that call a jam.
explanations.CALL: Closing the action cheaply against a range that misses most flops. Pairs and suited broadways that can make a strong pair without needing depth.
explanations.FOLD: Offsuit hands with one high card are the classic Big Blind leak, and shorter stacks make them worse: dominated when they hit, no room to maneuver when they miss.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. CO opens to 2.5bb, folded to Hero in the BB. 3-bet to 9bb, call 1.5bb more, or fold.

explanations.RAISE: A 25% opening range is wide enough to 3-bet for value with hands that would be behind against UTG, plus the suited wheel aces as the short-stack bluff.
explanations.CALL: A wide call is still right here - we close the action at a great price against a range that misses most flops.
explanations.FOLD: Hands with no suit, no connection and no high card. At 40bb there is nothing to be made of them later.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. BTN opens to 2.5bb, SB folds, Hero is in the BB. 3-bet to 9bb, call 1.5bb more, or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 88+, ATs+, AJo+, KQs, KJs, QJs, A5s-A2s, KTs, JTs, T9s

explanations.RAISE: The Button opens widest, so this is our widest 3-bet. Letting that range see a cheap flop in position is the biggest Big Blind mistake at any depth.
explanations.CALL: Getting 3.5-to-1 closing the action against the loosest range at the table. Folding too much is still a far bigger leak than calling slightly too wide.
explanations.FOLD: A smaller fold range than against anyone else, but tighter than it would be at 100bb - the bottom of a Big Blind defence lives on implied odds that 40bb does not provide.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. SB opens to 3bb, Hero is in the BB. 3-bet to 10bb, call 2bb more, or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 77+, A9s+, ATo+, KQs, KJs, KTs, QJs, QTs, JTs, KQo, A5s-A2s, K9s, Q9s, T9s, 98s

explanations.RAISE: Blind versus blind against the widest range anyone opens, heads-up and in position. We 3-bet a lot: the SB has to fold or play a big pot out of position with a short stack behind.
explanations.CALL: Only 2bb more to see a flop heads-up in position. Almost anything with a suit, a connection or a high card continues.
explanations.FOLD: A very small fold range. Against an SB opening this wide, folding is the mistake.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. UTG opens to 2.5bb, folded to Hero in the SB with the BB still to act. 3-bet to 9bb, call 2bb more, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: JJ+, AKs, AQs, AKo, TT-77, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

explanations.RAISE: Out of position with the Big Blind behind, so mostly 3-bet or fold. Against UTG the value range is narrow and the 3-bet is committing.
explanations.CALL: A handful of hands strong enough to play a possibly multiway pot out of position. Short stacks make that worse, not better.
explanations.FOLD: Cold-calling out of position with a player left to act is the worst spot in the game, and 40bb removes the compensation of outplaying anyone later.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. MP opens to 2.5bb, folded to Hero in the SB with the BB still to act. 3-bet to 9bb, call 2bb more, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: TT+, AQs+, AKo, A5s-A4s, 99-66, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s, AQo

explanations.RAISE: Still mostly 3-bet or fold out of position, but MP's wider range lets us add a value hand and a wheel ace.
explanations.CALL: Pairs and suited broadways only. With the Big Blind behind and 40bb, anything weaker is a trap.
explanations.FOLD: Most hands. The price looks fair and the position does not.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. CO opens to 2.5bb, folded to Hero in the SB with the BB still to act. 3-bet to 9bb, call 2bb more, or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 99+, AJs+, AQo+, KQs, A5s-A3s, KJs, QJs
ranges.DEFEND: 99+, AJs+, AQo+, KQs, A5s-A3s, KJs, QJs, 88-55, ATs, A9s, KTs, QTs, JTs, T9s, AJo

explanations.RAISE: Against a 25% range we 3-bet considerably wider for value, with suited wheel aces making up the bluffing half.
explanations.CALL: Deliberately small. With the Big Blind behind, most continues should take the initiative rather than invite a multiway pot at a depth where we cannot outplay anyone.
explanations.FOLD: Out of position, a player still to act, and a range that still holds plenty of strong hands.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. BTN opens to 2.5bb, Hero is in the SB with the BB still to act. 3-bet to 9bb, call 2bb more, or fold.

ranges.RAISE: 77+, A9s+, AJo+, KQs, KJs, KTs, QJs, QTs, JTs, KQo, A5s-A2s, T9s, 98s
ranges.DEFEND: 77+, A9s+, AJo+, KQs, KJs, KTs, QJs, QTs, JTs, KQo, A5s-A2s, T9s, 98s, 66-22, A8s-A6s, K9s, Q9s, J9s, ATo, KJo

explanations.RAISE: The widest range we face, so the widest 3-bet we make. Out of position with a player behind, taking the pot down now or playing with the initiative beats flatting.
explanations.CALL: A small set of hands that flop well enough to defend without raising.
explanations.FOLD: Wide as the Button is, calling out of position with the Big Blind still to act needs a real hand at 40bb.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Hero opens UTG to 2.5bb, BB 3-bets to 9bb. Jam 40bb, call, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: QQ+, AKs, AKo, JJ, TT, AQs

explanations.RAISE: At 40bb the 4-bet is the stack. There is no 4-bet-and-fold, so the raising range is exactly the hands happy to get it all in against a Big Blind 3-bet.
explanations.CALL: Hands too strong to fold but not quite wanting 40bb in against UTG's own tight range. We see a flop with roughly 3.5 SPR.
explanations.FOLD: Everything else in an already tight opening range. Facing a 3-bet with 40bb there is no room to continue speculatively.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Hero opens MP to 2.5bb, BTN 3-bets to 8bb. Jam 40bb, call, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: QQ+, AKs, AKo, JJ, TT, 99, AQs, AJs, KQs

explanations.RAISE: The Button 3-bets wider than a blind would, which widens the hands that want 40bb in - but the jam is still value, not a bluff.
explanations.CALL: Pairs and suited broadways that flop well enough to defend in position-disadvantaged but low-SPR pots.
explanations.FOLD: Most of the opening range. Short stacks reward folding over fancy play.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Hero opens CO to 2.5bb, BTN 3-bets to 8bb. Jam 40bb, call, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: JJ+, AKs, AQs, AKo, TT, 99, 88, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, AQo

explanations.RAISE: A Button 3-bet against a CO open is wide, so the jamming range widens with it. JJ and AQs are happy to be all in against that range at this depth.
explanations.CALL: Hands that keep enough equity to see a low-SPR flop in position.
explanations.FOLD: The bottom of a 25% opening range, which has no way to continue profitably against a raise this large relative to the stack.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Hero opens CO to 2.5bb, BB 3-bets to 9bb. Jam 40bb, call, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: JJ+, AKs, AQs, AKo, TT, 99, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, AQo

explanations.RAISE: The Big Blind 3-bets from out of position, which tightens their range relative to the Button - but the jam is still the only raise available at 40bb.
explanations.CALL: Enough equity to take a flop in position with a low stack-to-pot ratio.
explanations.FOLD: Most of the opening range. In position is not enough compensation when the stack is this shallow.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Hero opens BTN to 2.5bb, SB 3-bets to 9bb. Jam 40bb, call, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: TT+, AQs+, AKo, A5s-A4s, 99-66, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, AQo, AJo

explanations.RAISE: Our opening range is very wide, so the SB 3-bets wide to attack it - which means the hands that want 40bb in reach further down than against an early-position 3-bet. The suited wheel aces are the one jam bluff that still works.
explanations.CALL: In position with a low SPR, a wide band of pairs and suited broadways can take a flop profitably.
explanations.FOLD: The bulk of a 45% opening range. Opening wide on the Button means folding a lot when it is raised.

charts.description: 6-Max Cash, 40bb. Hero opens BTN to 2.5bb, BB 3-bets to 9bb. Jam 40bb, call, or fold.

ranges.DEFEND: TT+, AQs+, AKo, A5s-A4s, 99-66, AJs, ATs, A9s, KQs, KJs, KTs, QJs, QTs, JTs, T9s, AQo, AJo

explanations.RAISE: The Big Blind attacks a Button open widely, so the jamming range stays wide. Suited wheel aces block the calls.
explanations.CALL: We have position and a low SPR, which lets a broad range of pairs and suited hands continue.
explanations.FOLD: Still most of the opening range - a wide steal cannot survive a raise this large relative to 40bb.
